questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Hostile
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Hospitable**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Hostile"** means unfriendly, antagonistic, or having an aggressive attitude towards others. (शत्रुतापूर्ण)

 
 
• **Example:** The hostile tone of his voice made it clear that he was upset.
 
 
 
• **"Hospitable"** refers to being friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers. (अतिथि सत्कार करनेवाला)
 
 
• **Example:** They were very hospitable and made us feel at home during our stay.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Hostile'** is **'Hospitable'**.

• **Antagonistic** (विरोधी): Showing opposition or hostility toward someone or something.
 
 
• **Example:** The two teams have always had an antagonistic rivalry.
 
 
 
• **Icy** (बर्फीला): Covered with ice or very cold in demeanor.
 
 
• **Example:** Her icy stare made him shiver with fear.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The project must be completed ________ the end of the week.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. by .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence indicates a deadline for the project.
 
• The word **“by”** is commonly used to specify the time limit within which an action must be completed.
 
• **“By”** is appropriate as it suggests that the project must be finished before or at the end of the week.
 
• Other options such as “on,” “at,” and “in” do not convey the correct meaning in the context of a deadline.

Correct sentence: *The project must be completed **by** the end of the week*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Prepositions:**

 
 
• **On:** Refers to specific days or dates. Example: The meeting is on Friday.
 
• **At:** Refers to specific points of time. Example: The train arrives at 5 PM.
 
• **In:** Refers to a period of time within which something occurs. Example: He will finish the work in two days.

questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with an adverbial usage error.

Dravid and / his team / beautifully entered / the competition.
questions.solution:
The incorrect part is: '1' i.e. beautifully entered .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains an adverbial usage error in the segment **"beautifully entered".**
 
• The adverb **"beautifully"** is used incorrectly here because it does not logically or contextually fit with the verb **"entered".**
 
• Adverbs should be used to modify verbs in a manner that is grammatically and contextually appropriate. For example, using an adverb like **"confidently"** or **"gracefully"** would make more sense depending on the context.

Correct sentence: *Dravid and his team **confidently **entered the competition.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adverb Usage:**

 
 
• An adverb modifies verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, describing how, when, where, or to what extent something happens.
 
• Example: She **quickly** finished her homework. (**Quickly** describes how she finished.)
 
 
 
• **Common Adverbial Errors:**
 
 
• Using an adverb that does not suit the verb it modifies.
 
• Example: Saying **"he beautifully ate"** is incorrect because "beautifully" does not logically describe the act of eating.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

As the news of the atomic attack reached Einstein, he __is becoming aware of__ the glaring horror of the abuse of atomic energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. became aware of .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence discusses a **past event**, "as the news of the atomic attack reached Einstein," which requires the **verb **to be in the **past tense**.
 
• The phrase "he is becoming" is in the present continuous tense and is grammatically incorrect in this context, as the sentence refers to a completed action in the past.
 
• The correct substitution is "became aware of," as it aligns the tense with the past narrative of the sentence.
 
• Using "became aware of" accurately conveys that Einstein realised the gravity of the situation at a specific point in the past.

Correct sentence: *As the news of the atomic attack reached Einstein, he **became aware of** the glaring horror of the abuse of atomic energy*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tense Consistency:** It is crucial to maintain consistency in tense usage within a sentence to avoid grammatical errors.
 
• **Present Continuous vs. Past Simple:** The present continuous ("is becoming") is used for actions happening at the moment of speaking, while the past simple ("became") is used for actions completed in the past.
 
• **Other options explained:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** "become the awareness" is grammatically incorrect and does not make sense in the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2:** "No substitution required" is incorrect because the original phrase "he is becoming aware of" does not fit the past context.
 
• **Option 4:** "will be aware of" is in the future tense and does not match the past context of the sentence.
